title: Conversation datasets
intro: Collection method changes what a conversation dataset can tell us. Counts below refer to the named release and unit.
takeaway: Observed logs show submitted usage; structured studies add participant feedback; authored or synthetic dialogues serve different purposes.

types.label: Structured study
types.description: Participants interacted under a study protocol.

datasets.name: WildChat-4.8M (pinned filtered release)
datasets.collection: Consenting users received free access to ChatGPT through a public chat service.
datasets.record: A stored conversation containing user messages and AI replies.
datasets.linkage: Hashed IP + browser headers allow tentative cross-conversation association; no verified participant identity.
datasets.limitation: Filtered to content not flagged as toxic by OpenAI Moderation or Detoxify; free-service users do not represent all AI users.
datasets.short: Observed chat logs · approximate cross-session linkage
datasets.count_note: The 4.8M name refers to the larger collection, not this 3.2M filtered export.

datasets.name: WildChat (2024 paper snapshot)
datasets.collection: The same free ChatGPT service, with explicit consent to collect and publish transcripts.
datasets.record: A conversation reconstructed from requests containing their prior history.
datasets.multi_turn: Yes; paper reports about 2.5 interaction rounds per conversation.
datasets.linkage: Hashed IP + headers are proxies; the authors do not supply confirmed user linkage.
datasets.license: Current WildChat card states ODC-BY applies retroactively.
datasets.supports: Understanding the original collection and published analyses.
datasets.limitation: The paper snapshot differs from current filtered downloads; its counts and distributions cannot be reused as the denominator for this hub.
datasets.count_note: The paper also contains a conflicting 1,009,245 count in §3; this row follows §2 and Table 1. The current legacy card export has changed again.

datasets.name: LMSYS-Chat-1M
datasets.collection: Vicuna demo and Chatbot Arena traffic with terms-of-use consent.
datasets.record: Conversation ID, model, transcript, language and moderation fields.
datasets.linkage: No released user ID or IP field in the documented schema. The reported 210K IP addresses describe collection, not public user linkage.
datasets.license: Custom LMSYS agreement; prohibits redistribution and embedding dataset content.
datasets.supports: Comparing naturally submitted requests across models.
datasets.limitation: Demo/Arena traffic is self-selected. Unsafe content is retained, and benchmark contamination was not removed.
datasets.count_note: The custom agreement permits research/commercial work subject to its conditions; this is not unrestricted open redistribution.

datasets.name: OpenAssistant OASST1 (ready export)
datasets.collection: Volunteers wrote both user and assistant roles, then ranked and labelled messages.
datasets.record: A message with parent_id and message_tree_id; branches represent alternative replies.
datasets.multi_turn: Yes; branching trees rather than one linear exchange.
datasets.linkage: Contributor user_id identifies authorship; it does not make a tree the lived conversation of one end user.
datasets.supports: Studying human-written assistant responses with ratings and alternative branches.
datasets.limitation: Authored for dataset construction, not passively recorded AI use. The all-tree export has 161,443 messages, a different scope.
datasets.count_note: HF train (84,437) + validation (4,401) equals 88,838 ready-export messages. Do not call these 88,838 conversations.

datasets.name: PRISM
datasets.collection: Participants completed a survey, prompted live LLMs, rated responses and provided feedback.
datasets.record: A conversation tree with user_id, alternative responses, ratings and survey linkage.
datasets.multi_turn: Yes; participants were asked to complete six conversations across three task types.
datasets.linkage: Explicit user_id joins each participant’s study conversations and survey. This is not months of everyday use.
datasets.license: Human text CC-BY 4.0; model responses CC-BY-NC 4.0 plus provider terms.
datasets.supports: Relating response preferences to participant profiles and comparing alternative model outputs.
datasets.limitation: Participants chose their own prompts within unguided, values-guided or controversy-guided tasks, then rated competing responses. This is not a record of everyday use over months.
datasets.count_note: The card reports 68,371 rated utterances (prompt–response–score triples), not 68,371 conversations.

datasets.name: UltraChat 200k (SFT splits)
datasets.collection: Two ChatGPT API agents played user and assistant; H4 subsequently filtered and edited the generated dialogues.
datasets.record: A generated dialogue with prompt_id and alternating role messages.
datasets.linkage: No real user identity or human interaction history.
datasets.supports: Instruction-tuning experiments with a defined synthetic source.
datasets.limitation: Cannot estimate what real users ask or how people respond to AI. These counts exclude separate generation-ranking splits.
datasets.count_note: This is a specified subset, not the original paper’s roughly 1.5M dialogue collection. The gen splits contain another 256,032 train / 28,304 test records.

studies.name: Three-week sycophancy experiment
studies.design: Randomized response-style conditions; repeated sessions and questionnaires from the same participants.
studies.scale: Study 4: 1,364 randomized participants; 12 sessions over 3 weeks.
studies.transcripts: No raw transcripts in the public repository files inspected.
studies.status: Study, not an open transcript corpus
studies.note: AI history resets between sessions. Multi-study total N=3,075 is not the longitudinal sample.

studies.name: Four-week chatbot experiment
studies.design: Random assignment across text/voice modes and conversation prompts; weekly questionnaires.
studies.public_material: Paper, methodological appendix and classifier definitions.
studies.transcripts: No raw transcripts in the linked public repository.
studies.note: Controlled study use differs from naturally collected logs. Avoid claiming that observed use–outcome associations prove harm.

studies.name: Character.AI chat-donation study
studies.design: One-time survey plus optional donation of existing chat histories, using a local browser export tool.
studies.public_material: Participant-level quantitative data, analysis code and donation-extension source.
studies.transcripts: Not public; repository explicitly states consent agreements do not permit sharing raw histories.
studies.note: Historical chat coverage is not a prospective follow-up study.

scope_notes: This comparison is a source review, not a reanalysis of every dataset.
Scale uses different units; do not compare row counts as though they were the same object.
Access conditions and provider terms should be checked again before reuse.
WildChat’s paper snapshot and this hub’s pinned filtered release have different denominators.
